claims.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
claims.evidence: A shortest cycle remaining in G-S is induced and even. If it had length at least 10, eight consecutive vertices would induce P8, so its length is 4, 6, or 8. Conversely, an FVS meets every such cycle. Each remaining component is a tree with diameter at most 6 and hence radius at most 3. Inclusion-minimality means restoring x creates a cycle through x; removing x from that cycle leaves a path between two distinct neighbors of x in one component.
claims.witness: The shortest surviving cycle and, for minimality, the cycle created by restoring x provide the required witnesses.
claims.search_method: Direct proof from shortest cycles, induced-path exclusion, tree diameter, and inclusion-minimality; disconnected and empty-set cases were checked separately.

claims.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
claims.evidence: By claim 0, FVS is exactly transversal of the hypergraph of induced C4, C6, and C8, which has rank at most eight and can be listed in O(n^8). Branching on an uncovered hyperedge gives at most 8^k nodes up to polynomial factors. For approximation, the union of a maximal vertex-disjoint family of these cycles hits every hyperedge; if the family has p members, every FVS has size at least p while the union has size at most 8p.
claims.witness: The branching recurrence is T(k)≤8T(k-1)+O(n^8), and a maximal disjoint short-cycle packing certifies the approximation bound.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the hitting-set reduction, branching coverage, running time, maximality argument, and packing lower bound from first principles.

claims.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
claims.evidence: Independent exhaustive enumeration of all bipartite chord sets on an ordered required path reproduced survivor counts 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0 for orders 1 through 15. Thus no qualifying graph has a 15-vertex simple path. Every root-to-leaf DFS path consequently has at most 14 vertices. Bags consisting of each vertex and all its DFS ancestors cover every edge, have connected vertex occurrences, and have size at most 14, proving treewidth at most 13. Standard fixed-width forest-connectivity DP then solves FVS polynomially.
claims.witness: The exhaustive survivor set at order 15 is empty; the preceding counts exactly match the claimed certificate.
claims.search_method: Enumerated every possible edge from each new ordered-path vertex to earlier opposite-parity vertices, rejecting precisely C4s and induced P8s, then independently checked the DFS decomposition argument.

claims.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
claims.evidence: In the ambient class of P8-free bipartite graphs, four-way branching finds a minimum C4-transversal X of size r in O(4^r n^{O(1)}). Claim 2 gives a width-13 decomposition of G-X; adding X to every bag gives width at most r+13. A nice-decomposition DP storing deleted bag vertices and the connectivity partition of retained vertices has 2^{O(r log r)} states and can reject exactly those introduce-edge or join combinations that form cycles. The sum of the search and DP costs is within the stated product bound.
claims.witness: A minimum C4-transversal X is the modulator witnessing treewidth at most r+13.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the iterative-deepening search, modulator augmentation, partition-state count, join-cycle test, and runtime composition. The P8-free bipartite scope was retained from the draft context and proof.

claims.claim: On a chain graph—one whose neighborhoods on a bipartition side are linearly ordered by inclusion—a maximum-gain induced forest for arbitrary rational vertex gains, with one specified vertex optionally forced retained or deleted, is constructible in O(n^2). Consequently, weighted Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on chain graphs, including half-graphs with unbounded C4-transversal number.
claims.evidence: In Ferrers order, a retained subgraph is cyclic exactly when at least two retained A-vertices each have at least two retained B-neighbors: nesting then supplies a C4, while every cycle supplies two such A-vertices. If q is the second retained B-position, exactly one earlier B is selected, later positive-gain B-vertices and low-degree positive-gain A-vertices are independent, and at most one high-degree A-vertex is retained. This proves the displayed O(n^2) case enumeration. Deletion preserves the chain property, and a bonus M>2Σ|w(v)| forces retention because a feasible retained singleton beats every solution omitting that vertex. Exact brute force matched the formula and forced-retention reduction on 20,793 small degree-sequence/gain instances.
claims.witness: For fixed second B-position q, the optimal set consists of the best earlier B, b_q, every positive later B and low A, and the best positive high A.
claims.search_method: Derived the forest characterization and optimization formula symbolically, checked forced states and signed gains, and exhaustively compared against all induced forests for small Ferrers graphs using exact rational arithmetic.

claims.claim: Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on graphs whose every block is a chain graph. This gives a direct exact algorithm for a P8-free subclass that can contain both C4 and an induced P7.
claims.evidence: Every cycle is contained in one block, and the block-cut incidence graph is a forest. Conditioning each articulation on retained/deleted status turns each child subtree contribution into a unary gain at that articulation. Claim 4 therefore computes each block-to-parent message with the parent articulation forced, while assigning each original articulation cost once avoids double counting. The supplied eight-vertex example has chain blocks, contains the stated induced P7 and a C4, and cannot contain P8 because its full induced graph is not a path.
claims.witness: For the example, x2-x1-a1-b1-a2-y1-y2 is an induced P7; its nontrivial block is K2,2 and its other four blocks are bridges.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the two-state block-cut dynamic program, checked cycle locality and cost accounting, and verified the boundary example edge by edge.

claims.claim: For every n≥2, the half-graph H_n is P5-free and has no false twins, yet its minimum C4-transversal has size n-2 and its treewidth is at least ⌈n/2⌉. Thus neither bounded C4-transversal number nor bounded treewidth follows from P8-freeness, even after excluding false twins.
claims.evidence: The two neighborhood chains are strict and nonempty, so all open neighborhoods are distinct. An induced P5 contains an induced 2K2, which nested neighborhoods exclude. If a C4-free retained set has second-smallest selected A-index j, it has at most n-j+2 selected A-vertices and at most j selected B-vertices, hence at most n+2 vertices; all B together with a_{n-1},a_n attain this. Thus the transversal number is n-2. With p=⌈n/2⌉, the indicated vertices contain K_{p,p}; contracting p-1 matching edges yields a K_{p+1} minor, proving treewidth at least p.
claims.witness: The maximum C4-free set B∪{a_{n-1},a_n} has n+2 vertices; the K_{p+1} minor uses p-1 contracted matching edges and the two unmatched endpoints.
claims.search_method: Proved the nesting bounds and minor construction for general n, then exhaustively checked P5-freeness, distinct neighborhoods, and transversal values for 2≤n≤6.

claims.claim: There are 2-connected C4-free P8-free bipartite graphs of unbounded order: the graph formed by m≥2 internally disjoint length-three paths between two common terminals has 2m+2 vertices.
claims.evidence: Every cycle must traverse two arms and therefore has length six, so no C4 occurs. Removing either terminal leaves a connected subdivided star; removing an internal vertex leaves connectivity through any other intact arm, so there is no cut vertex. An induced path avoiding both terminals has at most two vertices, one using one terminal has at most five, and one using both has one complete terminal-to-terminal arm plus at most one vertex beyond each terminal, hence at most six vertices. The order 2m+2 is unbounded.
claims.witness: For m≥3, x_1-u-x_2-y_2-v-y_3 is an induced six-vertex path attaining the general upper bound.
claims.search_method: Classified cycles, vertex deletions, and induced paths by terminal usage for arbitrary m; exhaustively checked 2≤m≤7.

claims.claim: The natural LP that assigns nonnegative vertex weights and requires total weight at least one on every induced C4, C6, and C8 has integrality gap at least 2-o(1) on P8-free bipartite graphs: on K_{n,n} its exact fractional optimum is n/2 while its FVS optimum is n-1.
claims.evidence: For n≥2, K_{n,n} is P4-free and its only induced cycles are C4s. An induced K_{a,b} is a forest exactly when min(a,b)≤1, so at most n+1 vertices remain and the integer FVS optimum is n-1. There are C(n,2)^2 C4 constraints, and each vertex occurs in (n-1)C(n,2) of them. Summing them yields Σx_v≥n/2, while x_v=1/4 attains equality. The ratio is therefore 2-2/n.
claims.witness: Uniform weights x_v=1/4 give the fractional solution; retaining one entire side and one opposite vertex certifies the integer upper bound n-1.
claims.search_method: Recomputed cycle and incidence counts, the summed LP lower bound, the uniform feasible solution, and the maximum induced-forest size using exact fractions for 2≤n≤10 and algebraically for all n≥2.

target_evidence: The source asks for a polynomial-time algorithm on every P8-free bipartite graph. The draft proves relevant structural facts, an FPT algorithm in solution size, an approximation, a bounded-treewidth result under C4-freeness, an FPT result in the C4-transversal parameter, and exact algorithms for chain-based subclasses. It also correctly demonstrates that the relevant parameters are unbounded on the full class. None of these results supplies a polynomial-time algorithm for arbitrary instances, and the writeup expressly disclaims full resolution, so PARTIAL is accurate.
